section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Indus Valley city famous for its Great Bath and well-planned granary is:
explanation: Mohenjo-daro (Sindh) is famous for the Great Bath and granary. Lothal is known for its dockyard, Kalibangan for ploughed-field evidence, Dholavira for its water-conservation system.

section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch46 — Ancient & Medieval India
subject: Social Studies
stem: Emperor Ashoka embraced Buddhism and adopted non-violence after the war fought at:
explanation: The Kalinga War (261 BCE) so moved Ashoka that he adopted Dhamma and renounced further conquest, as recorded in his Rock Edict XIII.

section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch47 — Modern India & National Movement
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Revolt of 1857 is often regarded by many Indian historians as the:
explanation: V.D. Savarkar and other nationalist historians termed 1857 the 'First War of Independence', decades before the Swadeshi and Non-Cooperation movements.

section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch48 — Indian & World Geography
subject: Social Studies
stem: The Deccan Plateau, covering most of peninsular India, is bounded by the Western Ghats on one side and which range on the other?
explanation: The Deccan Plateau is flanked by the Western Ghats (west) and Eastern Ghats (east), with the Vindhya-Satpura ranges marking its northern edge, not eastern boundary.

section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch50 — Civics: Government & Democracy
subject: Social Studies
stem: Which Fundamental Right is described as the 'heart and soul' of the Constitution, because it enables enforcement of all other rights?
explanation: Article 32 lets citizens approach the Supreme Court directly for enforcement of Fundamental Rights via writs — Ambedkar called it the heart and soul of the Constitution.

section: Social Studies (Paper-2) · Ch51 — Economics: Basic Concepts
subject: Social Studies
stem: The total monetary value of all final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given year is called:
explanation: GDP measures the value of final goods/services produced domestically in a year. Per capita income divides national income by population.
